body:
I understand your frustrations, but I think some of these issues might come down to misunderstandings or preferences rather than fundamental problems with Godot. Godot is open-source, so its development is driven by contributions from the community—not activists or some specific group. I'm not socially active or anything, but I love contributing to Godot

Here's a response for some of your complaints:

> The vertical scrolling speed in the UI is incredibly sensitive compared to my other apps and the setting 'navigation v scroll speed' doesn't do anything to it

If the setting doesn’t work, it could be worth filing a bug report. You may also contribute yourself as this is an open source community driven project.

> I cant use vim in your built in editor, the godot doesn't support the integration it requires

while Godot’s editor doesn’t natively support it, many devs use external tools like VS Code to great effect. And after all—workarounds exist, I'm pretty sure someone found some way to use vim with godot.

> You severly f'd up dictionaries by making them lists instead of hashmaps. This is just plain stupid and anyone with a programming background should clearly know why.

Dictionaries do function like hashmaps, but their behavior might differ from other languages. Languages do have their differences after all.


Godot thrives on user feedback and contributions, so if something isn’t working for you, there’s always room to collaborate or even fork the engine to suit your needs! 😊

This kind of rant issue is a breach of our Code of Conduct.

I get you are frustrated by some aspects of Godot (though some of your complaints are misguided, e.g. Dictionaries are indeed HashMap), but taking it on contributors with a troll post like this is not appropriate under any circumstances.

If you have concrete, actionable and constructive feedback, you can open issues or proposals for the relevant items. Please keep in mind to be respectful if you do so.
